title: Implement explicit model version selectors in API & SDK (tag / semver range / commit-hash)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need deterministic control over which model binary is used for inference while still benefiting from model updates and performance metadata. Current API allows specifying model names but does not clearly define resolution semantics for tags, semver ranges, or commit hashes. This leads to ambiguous rollouts, hidden regressions, and difficulty reproducing inference results.

Goal: Define and implement explicit version selector semantics in the Redwood API and SDKs so callers can request a model by: exact commit hash, semver range (inclusive/exclusive operators), or mutable tag (e.g., 'stable', 'latest'). Provide clear resolution rules, TTL/caching behavior for tag resolution, warnings for non-deterministic selectors, and a migration path for existing customers.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts a new optional field 'version_selector' with three mutually exclusive modes: 'commit', 'semver', 'tag'
Tag resolution documented: tags resolve to a canonical version id (commit SHA) at resolution time and that mapping is returned in the response metadata
Semver ranges follow npm-style semantics (e.g., '^1.2.0', '>=1.3.0 <2.0.0') and server selects the highest compatible published version
Commit hashes bypass semantic checks and must match an existing published version or return 404
SDKs expose helpers: Model.selector.commit(sha), Model.selector.semver(range), Model.selector.tag(name) and provide a deterministic 'resolved_version' in the response object
Long-lived tag caching: control via Cache-Control header and 'tag_ttl' per-tenant setting. Tag resolution must respect tenant-level override and default to 60s
Telemetry: every inference request logs resolution path (selector -> resolved_version) and flags when a tag changed between requests
Backward compatible: existing clients that pass 'model' string continue to work and implicitly use tag semantics but are logged as 'legacy-selector'
technical_notes: Server resolution order: if version_selector is present use it; otherwise interpret 'model' string as legacy tag selector and log deprecation
Tag mode: find latest published version with tag label, return resolved_version = publish_commit_sha; if tag has rollout policy (canary weights) include 'variant' metadata
Semver mode: maintain sorted index of semantic versions per model name using SemVer precedence rules; pick highest matching; tie-break by publish timestamp
Commit mode: validate sha exists in published manifest; if missing return 404 with guidance message
Cache: resolved mapping cached in in-memory cache with per-tenant TTL; invalidation occurs on publish events and when manual tag re-assignment occurs

SDK design: synchronous selector builder (no network call) plus resolver returned on first inference with resolved_version metadata; provide convenience 'pinResolvedVersion()' to persist commit in client config
Routing implications: consistent-resolved_version must be used for routing to model-serving pools to preserve KV cache compatibility across requests

Compatibility checks: when resolved_version's performance_profile is incompatible with requested runtime options (e.g., quantization profile mismatch) return structured warning with suggestion to adjust options or pin different version
migration_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): add version_selector to API and SDK but do not change default behavior. Release server + SDK with experimental flag
Phase 2 (warnings): after 3 weeks enable deprecation warnings for legacy 'model' string usage in logs/console
Phase 3 (opt-out rollout): provide tenant-level setting to opt into strict selectors (reject ambiguous requests). No tenant would be forced to change without explicit opt-in
Phase 4 (docs + examples): update quickstarts, add migration guide showing how to pin resolved commit hashes for reproducibility
test_plan: Unit tests for semver parser (edge cases: pre-release, build metadata, caret/range combos)
Integration tests: publish multiple versions, assign tags, and verify resolution for tag/semver/commit selectors
E2E tests: SDK selects semver range and receives resolved_version; ensure KV cache routing uses resolved_version to hit same serving host
Simulate tag re-assignment and confirm cache invalidation and telemetry emits 'tag_changed' event
Performance test: measure additional 95th percentile latency for first request using selector (resolution cost) and ensure it stays under 5ms at p95 for cached lookups
rollout_plan: Deploy resolution service behind feature flag runtime.selector_v1 on staging
Canary 10% of traffic for 48 hours with telemetry enabled, monitor resolution latency and error rates
Gradually increase to 100% after no regressions; enable SDK update prompt in console
Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams for eye on tag TTL defaults and on-prem schema compatibility
